explanations.1: This checks if Apache has the mod_headers module loaded before trying to use Header commands; if the module isn't available, Apache will ignore everything inside this block.
explanations.7: The 'always' keyword means this header gets sent even if there's an error, and the condition at the end (the part in quotes after 'always set') means this header only applies when the connection is using HTTPS.
explanations.21: The 'expr=%{HTTPS} == 'on'' at the end is a condition that tells Apache to only send this security header when the connection is secure (HTTPS); without it, the header wouldn't be sent over regular HTTP.
explanations.40: This entire line is commented out (starts with #) because it's powerful but risky—if the rules are too strict, your site might break, which is why the comments above warn you to test carefully before uncommenting it.
